speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, and weight loss, along with an enlarged supraclavicular lymph node. Can you tell me more about the abdominal pain—specifically, where is it located and does it radiate anywhere?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty swallowing or feel a lump in your throat, and have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as blood in your stool or black, tarry stools? I also need to know if you have had any recent fevers or if the pain is related to meals.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the fixed supraclavicular lymph node and significant weight loss, I need to rule out malignancy immediately. REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy of Supraclavicular Lymph Node.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CD20 positivity and high proliferative index strongly suggest a B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma. To confirm the specific subtype and guide treatment, I need to see the histology slides. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal fullness and tightening clothes suggest significant splenomegaly or organomegaly, which aligns with the extensive lymphadenopathy. I will now proceed with the diagnosis based on the CD20+ B-cell lymphoma findings and clinical presentation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
